chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Saeed al-A'raj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who comes for the prayer but does not find a place in the row. Should he stand alone until he finishes his prayer? He (peace be upon him) said: Yes, there is no problem if he stands parallel to the Imam.
ai.seo_question: What should a worshipper do if there is no space left in the prayer row during congregational prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific fiqh of *saff* (row) formation when the main line is full. It establishes that standing alone parallel to the Imam (*bi-hidha' al-imam*) is legally valid and preferred over standing behind the row or in a separate line, thereby preserving the spiritual and physical connection to the congregation (*jamāʿah*). This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on maintaining the integrity of the prayer formation even in crowded conditions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Saeed Al A’araj who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man goes over for the Salāt but he cannot find a place in the row. Can he stand alone until he is free from his Salāt?’ Heasws Yes. There is no problem even if he were to stand by the side (parallel) to the Imam’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sa‘id al-A’raj who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who comes to Salah (prayer) and does not find a place in the rows. Can he stand up alone until Salah (prayer) is complete? He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it is not an offense to stand parallel to the Imam.’”
